raw_answer_text:
A1: The clk signal (constant pulse pattern "p" throughout).
A2: All three (req, ack, done) rest at low (0) at the start.
A3: The request signal asserts first, followed later by the acknowledge signal.
A4: No — in the trace, ack only rises after req has already risen (ack goes high at the point where req is already high), so ack cannot assert before req does.
A5: The request line falls back to low only after the acknowledge signal has asserted (gone high), i.e., once the request has been acknowledged.
A6: The acknowledge signal falls back to low only after the request signal has already fallen back to low.
A7: The completion (done) signal indicates that the handshake cycle has finished; it asserts after the request has fallen (while acknowledge is still high) and then deasserts after acknowledge falls, marking the end of the exchange.
A8: (1) req rises (0→1), (2) ack rises (0→1), (3) req falls (1→0), (4) ack falls (1→0).
